depConstraints.description: The kernel is what every module is allowed to share, so it may depend on nothing that is not itself shared.
depConstraints.remediation: A kernel project reaching into a module has made that module part of the kernel; move the code, or move the dependency into the module.

depConstraints.description: A module's published surface may integrate with another module's published surface, its own internals, and the kernel.
depConstraints.remediation: Reach the other module through its layer:module surface rather than through anything it keeps internal.

depConstraints.description: Internals are private implementation. Cross-module integration is the published surface's job, not theirs.
depConstraints.remediation: Move the integration up into the module's layer:module surface, which is the only part allowed to name another module.

depConstraints.description: The deployable composes modules through their published surfaces; a module's internals are invisible to it.
depConstraints.remediation: Export what the app needs from the module's layer:module surface instead of importing the internal project.

depConstraints.description: Every module inherits the kernel's third-party dependencies, so the kernel takes none — Node built-ins included.
depConstraints.remediation: Keep the package in the module that needs it, or expose the capability from the kernel as an interface the module implements.

fitness.name: module-encapsulation
fitness.reason: The base profile's rows cannot express "its OWN module's internals": a tag list names tag values, and every module's internals carry the same layer:module-internal tag. So layer:module-internal reaching ANOTHER module's internals, and a published surface reaching another module's, are both permitted by the four rows above. This function is the half that reads the module: axis relatively — a dependency may leave its module only into something tagged layer:module, which is what a published surface is.
